I will keep my land in the usual `winter wheat + summer maize` rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the crop pattern I trust most because the land, machines, water, and weather all fit it. Wheat gives me a steady harvest first, then maize follows in the rainy season, so I can use one mu of land for two grain crops in one year. At my age, I do not want to chase complicated crops that need more labor, more market judgment, or more hand management. I will plant improved grain varieties, keep fertilization moderate instead of excessive, irrigate wheat more than maize, and use simple field management that I understand well and can finish on time. For wheat, I will plough and return straw because that helps the soil and gives me a better seedbed. For maize after wheat harvest, I will use no-tillage to save time and moisture. I will aim for stable yield, not the highest possible yield, because steady production is what I would choose for myself.

Sources I relied on for local fit: Quzhou County’s dominant system is winter wheat and summer maize, with county-level reports showing about 42万亩 wheat and 38万亩 maize and official “吨半粮” work centered on the wheat-maize double-cropping system; recent Hebei/Quzhou reports also cite demonstration fields around `725 kg/mu` wheat and `797 kg/mu` maize with about `14 kg/mu` nitrogen for each crop.
